subject: Learning Methods
title: The Pre-Sleep Routine
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on The Pre-Sleep Routine.

hook.text: Olympic athletes follow the same pre-competition routine every time. A pre-sleep routine works by the same principle.

buildup.text: A 30-minute wind-down routine trains your brain to recognize that sleep is approaching.

discovery.text: Effective routines include dim lighting, light stretching, reading a physical book, or journaling.

twist.text: Worrying in bed is the biggest sleep destroyer. Writing tomorrow's to-do list before bed reduced sleep onset time.

climax.text: Create a 30-minute routine: dim lights, write tomorrow's plan, read a chapter. Repeat nightly.

punchline.text: Same routine. Every night. Your brain learns to expect sleep.

quiz.question: Why does writing tomorrow's to-do list help with falling asleep?
options: Writing is physically tiring for the hand muscles
Externalizing worries onto paper reduces the need to hold them in working memory
To-do lists activate the planning center which triggers drowsiness
